speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with gait and limb ataxia and a significant medical history; to begin, have you experienced any recent changes in your vision, such as double vision or difficulty tracking objects, and do you have any known history of stroke or diabetes?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned clumsiness on the right side; does this ataxia worsen when you close your eyes or rely on sensory feedback from your feet? Also, regarding your significant medical history, are you currently taking any medications for neurological conditions like multiple sclerosis or Parkinson's disease?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI.

Your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab significantly increases your risk for PML, which explains your new onset ataxia. We need to immediately confirm this via MRI.
